(Search snippet content — CNN + Irish Times, late July–7 August 2026; own reporting language)

England drought and food prices, summer 2026:
- CNN (30 July 2026): an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit around half of England after months of scant rainfall following the driest July on record; England has now had three droughts in five years (2022, 2025, 2026). Last winter was England's eighth wettest on record (rainfall 42% above the long-term average), followed by exceptional heat.
- Farmers and experts warn of a direct knock-on effect on food supplies; repeated disruption to vegetable production could make healthy food less affordable and have lasting public-health effects. River/canal water levels have fallen and algae has spread as temperatures rise.
- Hosepipe bans have spread across much of the country; a new ban was imposed in the South West (South West Water) on 7 Aug, with more heat forecast for the following week.

The Irish Times (7 Aug 2026): global food prices hit a three-year high on the back of conflict and extreme weather.
